{"user":"I’m flying into Lisbon next month and only have one evening free. Can you suggest a great way to spend that evening, starting from the airport, with a simple plan and rough timing?","plus_response":"Absolutely. I’ll sketch a clean, timed plan for your one evening starting from the airport—and to make it genuinely work in practice, I’ll also include a couple of backup options and how to adjust based on whether you prefer views, food, or culture.

1) Get to the city (about 25–35 min)
- From Lisbon Airport (LIS) take the metro (Aeroporto → Saldanha, or otherwise connect) into central Lisbon, then get off near your first stop.

2) Golden-hour viewpoint (45–60 min)
- Head to Miradouro da Senhora do Monte (great panoramic views) or, if you prefer a shorter walk with a similarly strong view, Miradouro de Santa Catarina.
- Budget time for sunset and a quick drink/snack nearby.

3) Dinner in a lively neighborhood (75–90 min)
- Go to Chiado/Bairro Alto or Alfama for dinner. If you want seafood/Portuguese classics, aim around Chiado or along the Alfama side streets.
- Choose a place close to wherever you plan to end so you’re not commuting late.

4) Optional dessert + night stroll (30–45 min)
- After dinner, do a short walk: Rossio/Chiado areas for atmosphere, or a brief loop back toward Alfama.

Backups (so you can swap quickly)
- If it’s rainy: swap the viewpoint for a covered/indoor option in the Chiado area (or a quick museum stop), and keep dinner + a shorter stroll.
- If you arrive earlier than expected: add an extra viewpoint (one miradouro) before dinner.

If you tell me your arrival time (and whether you’re staying in the airport area, Baixa/Chiado, or elsewhere), I’ll lock the plan into an exact hour-by-hour schedule and pick the best miradouro/dinner neighborhood for your timing.","minus_response":"Sure—here’s a simple evening outline: take the metro into central Lisbon, head to a viewpoint (a miradouro) for sunset, then do dinner nearby, and finish with a short night stroll. You can figure out the exact miradouro and restaurant based on what you’re closer to when you land. I should leave the rest as an exercise to you."}
